subject: Request: Custom SLA & latency commitment for Acme Platforms — exception review
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acme.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-01T15:10:00Z
Subject: Custom SLA / latency request for enterprise contract

Laura —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement is asking whether Redwood can include a custom SLA for our platform deal. Two asks from Acme: 1) 99.95% monthly uptime for the hosted inference endpoints used by our primary product, and 2) p99 inference latency <= 100ms for the typical 64-token prompt we run (region: us-east-1).

We understand this is an exception but Acme is prioritizing low-latency availability for their go-live. Can you confirm whether this is feasible and what the commercial/technical implications are (dedicated capacity, price uplift, monitoring/auditability)? Procurement has a target signature date of 2026-03-20.

Attached: ACME_RFP_SLA_Reqs.pdf (high-level asks from procurement).

Appreciate a short runbook/commitment summary if possible — Jordan

--
Jordan Miles
Head of Platform Partnerships, Acme Platforms
jordan.miles@acme.com
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Looping in Sales/Prod/Legal/Finance — Jordan from Acme says procurement wants a 99.95% SLA + p99 <=100ms on their main workloads. See attached ask.

Quick asks:
- Vivek: what commercial path do you recommend (Dedicated vs Hosted SLA exception)?
- Marissa: is 100ms p99 realistic for typical LLM prompts at our current serving config? If not, what mitigations are available and what engineering/ops commitment would be needed?
- Rishi: any immediate legal concerns with offering an SLA exception that tightens uptime/latency?
- Steph: pricing/credit implications if we commit to a stricter SLA?

I want a short internal position by EOD 3/2 so we can respond to procurement. Thanks — Laura

laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-02T09:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Custom SLA / latency request for enterprise contract

Thanks Laura — quick take from GTM: Acme is strategic and this looks like a classic dedicated-capacity ask. Operationally we should propose Redwood Dedicated with reserved GPU pools + warm standby in a second AZ. Commercial options:

- Option A (preferred): Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commitment) + SLO at 99.95% for uptime. Price uplift ~35-45% over standard hosted rates depending on commit term.
- Option B: Hosted with premium support + traffic shaping; SLA limit ~99.9% and higher risk of latency violations during bursts.

For latency p99 <=100ms: that will be difficult on shared hosted paths. With Dedicated + pinned warm nodes and model quantization we can often get p50/p75 under 100ms, but p99 depends on sequence length and model choice. We'll need product and infra to confirm feasibility and propose a remediation playbook (caching, cold-start mitigation, smaller model variants).

Next steps: Marissa, can you validate technical feasibility by EOD 3/3? Steph: can you draft a sample uplift % and credit schedule for Option A so we can propose numbers to Acme? Rishi: legal caveats we should include?

-Vivek
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-03T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Custom SLA / latency request for enterprise contract

Vivek — technical assessment below. TL;DR: 99.95% uptime can be supported for Dedicated with a couple of constraints; p99 <=100ms for 64-token prompts is achievable only for very specific model/hardware configurations and with warm/pinned capacity and conservative request routing.

Details:
- Uptime: Dedicated pools with active-active across AZs + health checks + automated failover: measurable and supportable to 99.95% (we'll need to restrict maintenance windows and include a maintenance runbook).
- Latency: p99=100ms is aggressive. Factors: model size (7B vs 70B), seq length, batching policy, KV cache hit-rate, and inter-AZ latency. We can reach ~100ms p99 on a 7B-quantized model on A100-80GB with aggressive caching and single-model routing, but for larger models or multimodal inputs it will be much higher.
- Required commitments from Acme: pin to a specific model family, agree to max prompt length and concurrency tiers, commit to a reserved capacity profile, and accept a separate latency SLO measurement harness (we'll run side-by-side tests).
- Ops/engineering work: implement pinned warm nodes, reserve dedicated PCIe memory/workers, define emergency fallback to a slightly higher-latency but higher-availability model variant. Est. runway: 3-5 weeks for full validation and SLA runbook documentation.

Action items:
1) We can draft a technical appendix for the SLA that defines exact scope (models, seq lengths, latency measurement method). I'll prepare that by 3/6.
2) Need legal to limit liability and define credit mechanics. Rishi?

-Marissa (Product)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-04T10:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Custom SLA / latency request for enterprise contract

Appreciate the notes. A few legal guardrails to propose for any SLA exception:

1) Scope limitation: SLA applies only to endpoints and model variants explicitly named in the SOW; excludes third-party service outages and customer misconfiguration.
2) Measurement: agree a single measurement harness (we prefer Redwood-run active p99 tests + customer test vectors) and a reporting cadence.
3) Credits: use a capped credit schedule (e.g., credits = min(30% of monthly fee, calculated prorata) and explicit exclusion for force majeure).
4) Term & termination: require a minimum commitment term (e.g., 12 months) and right to renegotiate on sustained load > X QPS.
5) Auditability & logs: customer requires audit logs (retention window to be defined) — we can provide but must limit scope.

I'll prepare a redline to our standard MSA + a short SLA appendix for the proposed Dedicated option. Please send me the target SOW language and any measurement scripts if Acme wants to provide them.

-Rishi (Legal)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acme.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-07T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Custom SLA / latency request for enterprise contract

Jordan — thanks for the clarity and the RFP doc. We discussed internally and can provisionally support an exception for Acme with the following high-level position:

- Platform: Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) + active-active AZ failover.
- Uptime: target SLA 99.95% for the named endpoints in the SOW, subject to maintenance windows and exclusions (see attached).
- Latency: we can commit to a latency appendix scoped to a specific model family and prompt envelope; p99 <=100ms is feasible on smaller models (e.g., 7B-quantized) with pinned warm nodes — larger models may not meet that number.
- Commercial: premium for Dedicated (estimated uplift range 35-45% depending on term). Final numbers and credit schedule attached.

Attached: SLA_Draft_Acme_v3.pdf (technical appendix + credit schedule + legal caveats). Rishi will provide a redline to the MSA and Marissa will validate the exact model/measurement language. If this is acceptable in principle, can we schedule a 30-minute alignment call next week to finalize SOW and measurement details?

Target next steps:
- Acme to confirm which endpoints and model family to be covered by the SLA (Jordan).
- We will deliver a final SOW + redlined MSA + SLA appendix by 3/13.

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
